title: Mass Gap of Four-Dimensional Lattice Yang–Mills Theory for Every Compact Simple Group
description: Three papers and a Lean 4/Mathlib certificate. (1) Spacing-Uniform Lattice Inequalities Cannot Produce the Yang-Mills Mass Gap: a lattice gap uniform in lattice units forces vanishing continuum two-point functions; the open residual (Hypothesis R). (2) Mass Gap of Lattice Yang-Mills Theory up to the Dobrushin Ceiling: the sharp Hessian bound 4d, the sharp quarter for von Mises-Fisher laws on the three-sphere, and a lattice mass gap for four-dimensional SU(2) up to beta_W = 2/9. (3) Mass Gap of Four-Dimensional Lattice Yang–Mills Theory for Every Compact Simple Group (first posted as Hexagon preprint 2610.00341, 'in a Forest Gauge'): the gauge is fixed on straight lines meeting every plaquette once, so each free link has twelve partners; a unique free-boundary state, reflection positivity, exponential clustering and a transfer-matrix gap for SU(2) up to beta_W = 0.345 and SU(3) up to beta_W = 0.76 (plaquette blocks, constants certified in ball arithmetic); for every compact simple group, with kappa_G = h/(2 l_rho) the least Ricci curvature, a gap m_G(beta) = arccosh(1 + (kappa_G/(N|beta|) - 29/2)/12) for N|beta| < 2 kappa_G/29, past the curvature limit of the ungauged measure; and a conditional continuum step: a Dobrushin-Shlosman condition on one cube of fixed physical size, uniform along the continuum tuning, gives a mass gap in physical units for every continuum limit. What that requires: the cube condition holds at strong coupling, and it survives every perturbation of the action by finite-range terms whose Lipschitz constant is below an explicit threshold of order (2/n)^4, but for gauge-invariant perturbations in the small-field regime, with plaquette variables within eta of the identity, it needs cubes of side of order eta^(-1/2) and perturbations of order eta^2, so at a fixed cube size it is a strong-coupling statement; it forces the gauge-fixed links of a cube with trivial exterior to stay at mean distance at least (1-alpha)D/3 from the identity, so it fails at every fixed cube size once beta is large; for SU(2) a four-colour configuration with tetrahedral quaternions sharpens this to mean squared chordal distance at least 2(1-alpha) and mean distance at least 1-alpha, and for every compact simple group with the Hilbert-Schmidt metric of an irreducible representation the same colouring, through an SU(2) root subgroup and Schur's lemma, leaves at least the fraction 1-alpha of the Haar disorder, so the mean distance is at least (1-alpha)D/2; and bounds on single lines uniform in the exterior cannot give it (an SU(2) line with ten-step gap at most e^20 24^10 b^15 e^(-b/1280)). For SU(2) the cube condition needs n^4 >= 2(1-alpha) b/(5 L(b)), L(b) = 1 + log 24 + (3/2) log 9b, by a lattice Stokes inequality on discs of at most (n/2)(n/2+1) plaquettes, and a stationary flux configuration shows that the n^2 loss is of the right order; the continuum step holds for observables smoothed by the spatial gradient flow, whose transfer matrix is unitarily equivalent to the original one; these flowed fields, renormalised by one condition at a single physical separation, have reflection-positive continuum limits along subsequences for every tuning, with the renormalised two-point function the Laplace transform of a probability measure on [0, infinity], and a nontrivial limit exists if and only if the ratio of the two-point function of the smeared packet at a fixed physical separation to its reflected norm does not tend to zero; a lower bound on that ratio gives tight spectral measures after renormalising at that separation, and a one-slab upper bound on the Dirichlet form of the transfer matrix would give the lower bound (not proved). At every n the mean distance of the gauge-fixed links from the identity is at least (1/9) max(6b,1)^(-1/2). For a Gaussian field the averaged cube coefficient is computed exactly: it equals 1 at every size and stiffness when the field is massless, and with mass m it is at most 1-(5/6)^4 (m l)^2/((m l)^2+160) on cubes of physical side between l/2 and l. In the quadratic approximation of the forest gauge itself (the Gaussian field of the Wilson action with the forest links fixed) the class sums of the cube coefficients are at least the cube size at every n and every stiffness, so the cube condition fails there; for every SU(N) the cube condition needs n^4 >= 2(1-alpha) beta_W/(5 L_N(beta_W)) with L_N(b) = 1 + ((N^2-1)/2) log(81 pi^2 b) + N(N-1) log(12/11); in a periodic spatial box the reflected norm that renormalises the flowed observables is strictly positive; and no Bakry-Emery curvature argument for gauge-fixed SU(2) passes beta_W = 1/3; the slice criterion holds for two-dimensional SU(N) along its tuning; and for the free field, conditioning an energy packet on block averages leaves a fixed fraction of its variance at every lattice spacing, so the errors of a blocking route have to be measured in the reflected norm. For four-dimensional U(1) with the Villain action the cube condition fails at every cube size once beta is large, by the massless photon of Froehlich and Spencer, so a proof of the cube estimate has to use the non-abelian structure of the group. Posed for block averages in a block-rooted axial gauge (a spanning tree fixed in every block of side two), the quadratic approximation has a constrained gap 1/52 in every volume, its cube responses are localised by a Combes-Thomas estimate, and the block-constrained cube condition holds at every coupling for cubes of side at least 2 10^15/alpha, one step of averaging bounds the cube coefficients by the constrained ones plus those of the averages, which carry at least the coarse quadratic form at every scale; for the group-valued links themselves, with the straight path between block roots as coarse link, the free links satisfy D^2 <= 224 Q for every compact matrix group and all fields, the conditional partition functions obey two-sided bounds and the fluctuations around flat paths are O(1/beta) per link uniformly in the volume, but the path map does not compose (thin paths give fine to coarse energy ratio s sin^2(pi/2s)), and for every compact connected group no continuous covariant block map treats the transverse positions alike, since the homology matrices of the slice links in a maximal torus add up to the identity, and a cut-off of Balaban's averaging operation (the mean of the sixteen paths in the logarithmic chart at the straight path, switched to the path map at large fields) is continuous, covariant and coercive for every field with explicit one-step constants and agrees with the block averages to first order, breaking the transverse symmetry only at large fields; on fields with values in a maximal torus whose curvature stays small at every scale the k-fold cut-off average composes, with the coarse curvature the exact mean of the sixteen 2x2 fine fluxes, the energy nonincreasing at every scale and the thin paths contracted to coarse energy at most 18 pi^2/s^2 (the path map leaves 24); for every compact group the commutators of the cut-off average are bounded by the square of the local curvature, so on fields whose curvatures at the successive scales have a small sum sigma it composes with energy growing at most by exp(12060 sigma), which holds at every scale when eta_0 A_0 <= 2 10^-10 rho_G^2; while straight-path block averages in the forest gauge leave one class of lines invisible and fail at every size (with J. Lockwood's report); under the SU(2) Wilson measure, by reflection positivity and the chessboard estimate, a set A of unit cubes contains bad plaquettes with probability at most q^|A|, q = exp(6(log beta_W + C_0) - beta_W rho^2/16), so the clusters of bad cubes have vanishing physical size in probability and the cut-off is active only within two lattice spacings of them, while bad plaquettes are present along the one-loop tuning and a frustrated exterior makes a plaquette bad with probability tending to one; decay with constants of the renormalised correlations of a spanning set of observables also gives a gap for every continuum limit; the composition is local, the defects spread by at most three spacings of the current scale per step, and the cut-off average carries the field through the clusters up to a coarse spacing of order (beta_W/log beta_W)^(1/4) a, the order of the cube side that the cube condition needs; composition across the remaining scales and the crossover remain open. The cube estimate and the existence of the continuum limit are not proved, so the continuum Yang-Mills existence and mass-gap problem remains open. Lean: 86 theorems and lemmas, no sorry, standard axioms only.
